summary: Daylight-saving boundary caused missing prorated free-tier credit for cross-region batch-embed job
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports an unexpected negative provisional balance and missing prorated free-tier credit on their finalized invoice for a bulk embedding job that spanned the US DST transition. Impact:
- PixelFlow saw a -$84 provisional adjustment and autopay failed on 2026-03-09 invoice finalization.
- The batch embed ran across us-east and eu-west and the scheduler split work across hour boundaries that crossed the DST boundary for the org's billing tag.
Environment:
- prod, dedicated capacity, regions: us-east-1 (primary), eu-west-1 (fallback).
Steps to reproduce (as reported by customer):
1) Schedule a large batch-embed job that starts 2026-03-08 22:30 UTC and runs until 2026-03-09 02:15 UTC.
2) Job shards route between us-east and eu-west workers.
3) Observe invoice provisional lines and autopay failure on 2026-03-09.
Observed behavior:
- Prorated free-tier buffer credit was applied to the earlier hourly window but not to the window that shifted due to DST rules for the customer's org timezone tag.
- Postbacks from eu-west arrived with hour tags that did not align with the aggregator's UTC-windowing logic, producing a split-hour attribution and eventual negative provisional balance.
Expected behavior:
- Free-tier prorate should be applied consistently independent of DST transitions; hour windows used by postback aggregator and billing pipelines should align and be anchored in UTC to avoid double-split attribution.
Logs & evidence provided by customer:
- Customer provided job IDs: job-pixelflow-20260308-9, postback fingerprints for two shards, and a screenshot of the invoice line showing -$84 provisional adjustment.
- Packet captures and timestamps included in the customer attachment (sensitive) and uploaded to secure support artifact store.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Support (Aisha): Acknowledged receipt and escalated to Billing & SRE. Asked for job IDs and invoice PDF. Customer provided artifacts same day.

2026-03-11 - Billing (Marco): Initial hypothesis: postback aggregator windowing misaligned for tags using localized timezone. Pulling aggregator logs for the billing window 2026-03-09T00:00Z-2026-03-09T04:00Z.

2026-03-12 - SRE (Chen Li): Found that eu-west postbacks carried hour_tag=2026-03-09T01:00+01:00 while aggregator normalized tags to local org timezone, causing one shard to be double-split across adjacent hourly buckets.

2026-03-12 - Support (Aisha) -> Customer: Requested permission to view org's timezone tag mapping and asked if they ran any overlapping scheduled jobs. Customer confirmed no manual overlap; they use local timezone mapping in Console (Europe/Paris).
2026-03-13 - Billing (Marco): Applied provisional credit to offset negative balance while fix is implemented; awaiting confirmation that autopay can be retried. Noted follow-up actions scheduled.
investigation_notes:
Hypotheses:
- Postback aggregator used org-local timezone mapping for some regions and UTC anchoring for others after a recent deploy (scheduler PR-3065) causing window misalignment.
- DST boundary caused hour_tag normalization to produce different hour boundaries for eu-west (CET/CEST) vs aggregator UTC buckets.
Findings:
- Aggregator logs (job-pixelflow-20260308-9) show three postbacks with timestamps 2026-03-09T00:58:12+00:00, 2026-03-09T01:03:04+01:00, 2026-03-09T01:58:50+01:00. Aggregator normalized second and third to local offsets resulting in split attribution.
- Billing pipeline assumes hour windows are inclusive of UTC-based boundaries; mismatch introduced during rollout of build that added 'local-hour-tag' for console display, but postback pipeline unintentionally used it for aggregation.
- No evidence of duplicate tokens or retry storms. Token metering looks consistent with expected counts.
Related code references: PRs linked above; scheduler change that introduced local tagging: PR-3065 (rolled back in staging but partial migration to prod happened on 2026-03-07).
workaround: Applied a provisional invoice credit equal to the negative provisional line (-$84) to allow autopay to succeed. Recommended customers schedule large cross-region batch jobs entirely within a single UTC/hour window until fix deploy. Support toggled a temporary postback normalization flag for PixelFlow to force UTC windowing.
resolution: Temporary mitigation: provisional credit applied and postback normalization flag set for PixelFlow org to force UTC anchoring. Long-term fix: change aggregator to ignore localized hour tags for billing aggregation and use server-side UTC truncation of timestamps; regression test added for DST boundary jobs. Patch PR-4287 prepared to normalize postback timestamps to UTC at ingestion and PR-3120 updates scheduler tagging docs. Deployment targeted for 2026-03-18 with monitoring alert added.
follow_up_actions: Deploy PR-4287 to prod to normalize postbacks to UTC at ingestion (owner: Billing team) - target 2026-03-18
Add end-to-end regression test that simulates DST-transition spanning batch jobs (owner: QA) - target 2026-03-16
Audit recent canary rollouts for other orgs with local timezone tags and flag any with overlapping windows (owner: SRE) - target 2026-03-15
Document fallback for customers that require localized hour display vs billing UTC anchoring in Console docs (owner: Docs) - target 2026-03-22
resolution_status: Partial - provisional credit applied and temporary flag set; permanent fix pending deployment
customer_communication: 2026-03-13 - Support: Notified PixelFlow that provisional credit has been applied and autopay retried successfully. Explainer: DST boundary caused split-hour attribution; long-term fix will ensure billing uses UTC anchoring and avoid similar cases. Customer asked for an audit of prior month runs; billing agreed to perform audit and provide results by 2026-03-17.
